title: The Adventures of Frank Race
paragraphs: Adventure-detective series about former wartime intelligence operative Frank Race, who becomes an investigator and travels into cases involving murder, espionage, theft, and international intrigue.

Complete 43-program syndicated adventure-detective run about former OSS operative Frank Race and partner Mark Donovan. Program numbers 1-43 are stable; dates vary by market, so the frozen May 1949-Feb 1950 chronology is treated as a reference syndication schedule rather than a universal first-air sequence.
GRH documents the program through East Coast reference syndication schedule (May 1, 1949 to February 19, 1950) and West Coast resyndication schedule (June 5, 1951 to March 25, 1952).

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are director) (performer on 43 recordings), Buckley Angel (writer (performer on 42 recordings), Ivan Ditmars (organist on 42 recordings, composer on 1 recording, music on 1 recording, and performer on 1 recording), Joel Murcott (writer (performer on 42 recordings), Tony Barrett (performer on 42 recordings), Art Gilmore (announcer on 41 recordings), and Bruce Eells (producer on 40 recordings, director on 1 recording, and writer on 1 recording).
The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.6a65471e0dd3a5b5|Broadcasters Program Syndicate]] (syndicated by).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include international adventure and dangerous assignments, private investigation and insurance cases, murder and violent crime, international travel and foreign settings, theft, smuggling and stolen property, and espionage and postwar intelligence.

Adventure-detective series about former wartime intelligence operative Frank Race, who becomes an investigator and travels into cases involving murder, espionage, theft, and international intrigue.

Complete 43-program syndicated adventure-detective run about former OSS operative Frank Race and partner Mark Donovan. Program numbers 1-43 are stable; dates vary by market, so the frozen May 1949-Feb 1950 chronology is treated as a reference syndication schedule rather than a universal first-air sequence.

GRH documents the program through East Coast reference syndication schedule (May 1, 1949 to February 19, 1950) and West Coast resyndication schedule (June 5, 1951 to March 25, 1952).
